newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian share prices rise in featurless market.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian share prices rise in featurless market.

text.p: Egyptian shares rose on Monday in quiet trade still affected by the holiday season, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index added 0.98 points to 384.12 points. Turnover was less than average at 42.55 million pounds ($12.5 million).

"The market is still very quiet but prices are expected to go up next week," said Jihan Talaat of EFG/Hermes. The market is expected to have a three-day weekend this week to celebrate the start of the Islamic new year.

Mohammed Abdullah, Intercapital managing director, told Reuters that foreign investors were staying awary from the Cairo market until prices became cheaper and were waiting for the government start selling utilities and for more private, closed firms to turn public.
The traditionally stable cement sector slipped a bit but managed to stand up to the market's general downtrend.
Helwan Portland Cement is the most important at present because "it is one of the cheapest," said Abdullah.
It was the most active share, ending 0.55 pounds up at 78.05 after shares worth 4.5 million pounds traded.
Mills were more sharply affected. "No one wants to buy in millers now," Talaat said.
"Mills are not attractive anymore because the private sector is entering the milling sector as producers and it is better than the public sector in terms of marketing," Abdullah said.
He said East Delta Flour Mills, which increased its production capacity, could be an exception. The share closed 0.5 pounds higher at 74 pounds.
Egyptian American Bank (EAB) was the second most active share, but ended 3.5 pounds down at 143.5 pounds, with 3.3 million pounds worth of trade.

Heliopolis Housing and Development broke the 490- pound barrier during the session for the first time in more than a month. "This is an indication that there is cash that wants to come in but is waiting for the right time," said Abduallh.
The share ended 6.25 pounds down at 485.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 559.91 points from 557.26 points on Sunday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 274.94 from 274.58.
Out of the 88 shares traded, 31 advanced, 36 declined and the remaining 21 closed unchanged.
